brief: A herb planter of three cells side by side, each with a bin that drains.

requirements.requirement: Herb planter of three cells side by side
requirements.evidence: Three full bases at -1,0, 0,0 and 1,0 in a side-by-side row (check_build shows one group [-1,0, 0,0, 1,0]), each filled with soil and planted with a herb: basil, mint and parsley.

requirements.requirement: Each cell has a bin that drains
requirements.evidence: bin:-1,0,0~hex-bin-full-drain, bin:0,0,0~hex-bin-full-drain and bin:1,0,0~hex-bin-full-drain (hex-bin-full-drain, 'Bin, full depth, drained') placed in all three cells. Note: drainage is the bin floor's shape; the configurator checks fit only, not waterproofing or actual water flow.

finish.summary: A three-cell side-by-side herb planter: three full bases joined, capped and bolted (14 end caps, 2 joint bolts), each carrying a full-depth drained bin (hex-bin-full-drain) filled with soil and planted with a harvest-size herb — basil, mint and parsley. check_build passes with meshClash clear.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
